content: The Aurum Institute in South Africa, represented by Gavin Churchyard, has received significant funding for tuberculosis (TB) research and implementation projects. These include grants from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to evaluate the national rollout of Xpert MTB/RIF, funding from UNOPS for TB screening in peri-mine communities, and support from the South African Department of Health for community-based TB screening using symptoms and Xpert MTB/RIF. Additional funding was provided for TB screening in correctional facilities using digital chest radiography and computer-aided detection, as well as for evaluating chest radiography screening in primary health clinics and prisons. Elizabeth Corbett, affiliated with the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine and the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, has received substantial research support from the Wellcome Trust. Her projects include HIV self-testing and TB active case finding in urban settings, as well as systematic reviews on behavior change and systematic screening in health facilities. She has also been involved in international presentations and collaborations with organizations such as FIND and WHO. Knud Lönnroth, from the Karolinska Institute in Sweden, has received grants for research on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of TB community screening in high-burden settings like Nepal and Vietnam. He has also worked on TB screening in migrants in low-incidence settings in Europe, supported by funding from the Swedish Heart and Lung Foundation, the Swedish Research Council, and the EU Horizon 2020 program. He has reviewed protocols for computer-aided detection (CAD) systems used in TB screening. Guy Marks, President of the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease, has led trials on TB control funded by public research grants from NHMRC Australia. He has conducted studies using Xpert MTB/RIF for TB screening, though the manufacturer did not fund this work. Helen Ayles, a member of the Global Fund Technical Review Panel, has led a consortium studying the impact of active TB case finding strategies for TB and HIV, funded by EDCTP. Delft Imaging, a partner in the consortium, provided in-kind services, including CAD software and experimental radiography units. Due to her involvement with Delft, she was recused from sessions on CAD product recommendations. Connie Erkens, from KNCV in the Netherlands, declared involvement in a study on latent TB infection (LTBI) screening in migrants, which received diagnostic kits from Qiagen. Andrew Kerkhoff, from the University of California, San Francisco, collaborated on a review of TB screening in people living with HIV but received no funding for this work. Claudia Denkinger, Sandra Kik, Stefano Ongarello, and Morten Ruhwald benefited from free access to CAD software and technical advice from companies like Delft Imaging, qXR, and Lunit Insight CXR for research purposes. These software products were included in the analysis for WHO TB screening guidelines. Katherine Robsky declared research support for projects on TB transmission in urban Ugandan communities and spatio-temporal patterns of TB in sub-Saharan Africa. She has also authored systematic reviews on TB diagnostics and screening tests for WHO guidelines. Karen Steingart has consulted and conducted research on TB diagnostics, including systematic reviews on nucleic acid amplification tests and lateral flow urine assays for TB detection. She has also provided mentoring and technical support for Cochrane Reviews and guideline development. The WHO Guideline Development Group (GDG) and External Review Group (ERG) members completed declarations of interest forms, which were evaluated for potential conflicts. Intellectual conflicts were not considered grounds for exclusion, as expertise was deemed essential. Biographies of GDG members were made public alongside the 2019 guideline update. Some members declared interests judged not to conflict with the guidelines' objectives, while others were recused from specific discussions due to potential conflicts.
